To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RIG I mediated innate immune response against DNA viruses is regulated by post translational modifications of RIG I and its downstream molecules and lncRNAs.
ubiquitination, SUMOylation, phosphorylation and lncRNAs regulate RIG I mediated signaling for interferon induction during viral infection.
RIG I mediated signaling is regulated by post translational modifications of its adaptor proteins such as ubiquitlation, phosphorylation and adp ribosylation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the regulatory mechanisms of nucleic acid sensor mediated innate responses during viral infection, with a particular focus on the role of ubiquitination, lncRNAs and other post-translational modifications in innate signaling.
the regulation of signaling mediated by innate sensors for interferon induction during viral infection.
the molecular mechanisms of the host innate immune system in response to viral infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nucleic acid sensors are activated and regulated by post translational modification and lncRNAs to evoke innate immune responses.
nucleic acid sensors are tightly regulated by various post-translational modifications including ubiquitination, SUMOylation, acetylation and ADP-ribosylation, as well as long noncoding RNAs.
the innate immune system is regulated by many different mechanisms to ensure a proper response to invading viruses and to protect the host from excessive and harmful responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the regulation of RIG-I mediated signaling is achieved at the level of nucleic acid sensor activation by ubiquitin modification, at the level of signaling mediator recruitment and activation by ubiquitin and SUMO modification and at the level of lncRNA dependent recruitment of signaling mediators.
RIG-I and its adaptor MAVS are regulated by post translational modification, such as ubiquitlation, phosphorylation and SUMOylation, to modulate their signaling.

the innate sensors and its downstream signaling mediators are regulated by various post translational modifications and lncRNAs, and the regulation of innate sensors is critical for the host virus interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the innate immune response is tightly regulated by a variety of mechanisms, and the regulatory mechanisms are also regulated by the innate immune response itself.
The role of long non-coding RNAs in
the innate immune signaling is finely regulated by a number of post translational modifications, including ubiquitination, SUMOylation, phosphorylation, and ADP ribosyaltion.
lncRNAs can be a new class of regulator for innate immune responses and viral infection.
